decide which shard a unit lands in. A stale figure costs balance and nothing else:
assign() is total over units() whatever this file says, so no unit can run twice or
not at all because a number here is wrong. That is why check_counts.py does not police
it -- that checker guards numbers DERIVED FROM THE CORPUS, and a second on one machine
is not one of them.
THESE ARE THE RUNNER'S FIGURES, RE-DERIVED FROM CI RUN 34162261372 (7 Sep 2026), AND THE
FIRST SET WERE NOT. Measured on a 4-core container the table's TOTAL was right to 0.2%
-- 2,503 s against CI's 2,499 -- and its DISTRIBUTION was wrong enough to cost four
minutes of wall clock: the six shards came back 306, 315, 346, 423, 465 and 645 s against
a predicted flat 421. Two opposite errors cancelled in the sum. The per-file sweep ran
three files at a time, so contention inflated most of them (shards 4-6 landed at
0.73-0.82 of prediction); and the CP-SAT-bound files are much slower on a smaller runner
(shard 3 at 1.62). AN AGGREGATE THAT AGREES IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT THE PARTS DO, and only
the aggregate had ever been checked.
Provenance of each figure, because they are not all the same kind of measurement:
- the checkers, and tests/test_score.py: EXACT per-unit CI figures. Shard 1 held that
one file alone, which is the only shape the refresh block emits a per-file time for.
- every other test file: its local figure scaled by ITS OWN SHARD's measured ratio of
CI time to predicted. That is a GROUP measurement spread over a group, so a single
file inside it may still be wrong; what is right is each shard's total.
